title: Epidemiology of Large Language Models: A Benchmark for Observational Distribution Knowledge

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the model to predict real-world conditional probabilities of various outcomes (e.g., employment, health, education, occupation) by sex, and comparing these predictions to ground-truth population datasets. The study also explicitly compares model performance on tasks containing 'sex' as a protected attribute versus non-sensitive tasks to evaluate the impact of safety-oriented debiasing.

Prompting the model to predict real-world conditional probabilities of outcomes (e.g., crime statistics, drug use, health) by race, comparing predictions to ground-truth census and survey data, and evaluating whether fairness/safety alignments degrade statistical accuracy on race-related prompts.

Eliciting model predictions on conditional distributions of real-world outcomes (such as health conditions, substance use, and consumer finances) based on age groups, and comparing them to national survey datasets.

Testing the model's knowledge of empirical distributions regarding income levels and educational attainment across different population groups using likelihood and question-answering prompting strategies.

Evaluating the model's ability to accurately reflect real-world distributions of political views and party affiliations conditioned on demographic factors like age, race, and education using data from the General Social Survey.
